ceramic.snippet:
Total revenue for Q1 2026 reached $549 million, a substantial 22% increase compared to the same period last year. A significant driver of this growth was Atlas revenue, which surged by 26% year-over-year. Atlas now represents a substantial 72% of MongoDBs total revenue, underscoring the strong adoption of its cloud-based platform.

 MongoDB demonstrated strong cash generation in Q1 2026. Operating cash flow reached $110 million, with free cash flow at $106 million. The company maintains a robust balance sheet, holding $2.5 billion in cash and equivalents. This strong financial position provides significant flexibility for future investments and strategic initiatives.

 Looking ahead, MongoDB provided optimistic revenue guidance. For Q2 fiscal year 2026, the company expects revenue to be between $548 million and $553 million.

 MongoDB noted some softness in Atlas consumption during April, attributed to macroeconomic volatility, though consumption rebounded in May. The non-Atlas business is expected to decline in the high single digits for the year. The company also anticipates a $50 million headwind from multiyear license revenue in the second half of the fiscal year.

 Mike Berry, CFO, addressed questions on managing and communicating metrics for a consumption-based model. He affirmed that MongoDB already provides relevant metrics to investors, such as consumption and customer growth. Berry intends to focus on capital structure, cash flow generation, and improvements in operating margins. More detailed insights on these areas will be shared at the upcoming MongoDB.local NYC event.

 Dev Ittycheria offered insights into the competitive landscape, specifically regarding Snowflake and Databricks moves towards PostGres. He noted these moves validate the critical importance of operational data stores, particularly for AI applications. Ittycheria emphasized the inherent difficulty in building an Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) store.

- **The back-half acceleration stopped being a promise and became a print.** Product revenue of $996.8M grew 26.2%, or 27.7% adjusting for the leap-day lap, against a guide that implied 21.3%. Three months ago the full-year bridge required the last three quarters to grow 24.3% after a Q1 guided at 21.3%. It now requires the last two quarters to grow 24.3% after a first half running at 25.7%. The unverifiable part of the guide has largely been converted into delivered revenue, though net revenue retention slipped again to 124%, which is the exact floor management has verbally defended.
